FOREWORD
This

Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Meteorological lnstruments Sectional Committee, had been approved by the Basic& Production Engineering Division Counci 1.

The deposition of dew is essentially a nocturnal phenomenon. During clear nights with calm or low wind speed conditions, the ground as well as its environment exposed to sky loses heat due to radiation. When its temperature tills below the saturation temperatttre of the surrounding air, water condenses and deposits as dew, Dew is very crucial for the plants for their unhindered growth when seasonal rainfall is rather negligible. It is an important source of moisture to plants especially in arid and semi-arid climatic zones, which receive low q,uantum of rainfall. 1n some areas, the formation of dew itself forms an important secondary source of moisture'to the soil in the same order of magnitude as the rainfall of that place especially during non-rainy season. The fact is now widely recognized by the agricultural scientists. Dew is responsible for the spread of many plant diseases, surface soil moisture and thus affects the world economy in variety of ways. It is an important factor in microclimate as well as in weather forecasting. Measurement of accumulation of dew is now becoming an increasing demand for planning several agricultural operations and evolving new crop strains for hydrological or hydro meteorological studies. Study of dew has attracted the attention of plant breeders, plant physiologists and agronomists the world over. Dew is usually hydroscopic and is expressed in grams of moisture deposited per 100 cm2 of the exposed surface area or generally in millimetres of dew. One millimetre of condensed moisture in the form of dew corresponds to 10 g of dew deposited/100 cm2. While preparing this standard considerable assistance had been provided by lMA Hyderabad. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2: 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'. The number of significant piaces retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

This standard specifies the requirements of dew gauge for the measurements of dew. 2 DESCRIPTION 2.1 The general structure of the dew gauge shall be as shown in Fig 1.

wood coated with red oxide paint, which favours retention of dew deposit on them. During the dew season, the dew gauge is exposed on a suitable stand at about sunset and the size, form and distribution of dew deposited during the night are observed before the sunrise next day. IS 15253:2002 and IGWsurfaces of the block are compared with a series of standard full-scale photographs of dews types. The photographs bear the dew scales 1 to 8 and the dew scales are converted into equivalent amount of moisture in millimetres by a suitable table. 3 MATERIAL 3.1 Dew Gauge The dew gauge shall be made of suitable wood having the following properties: a) Having rigidity and strength with no distortion or deformation or any other deterioration when exposed to very low temperature conditions in the open air while at the same time being light in weight. Freedom from attack of animals, birds, insects or fungoidal life. Smooth surface finish to ensure uniform coating of good quality of red oxide paint. Low thermal conductivity so as to minimize the loss of evaporation. Material, which necessarily differs in its thermal properties from the surrounding air. Material shall be as simple as possible and shall preserve the dew until such time as an observer can conveniently go outside to record it. brass screws exactly at the heights of 50 mm, 250 mm, 500 mm and 1000 mm from the ground level. 3.2.2 The supports and clamping arrangements shall be painted with sufficient coating of white rubber paint to prevent corrosion or absorption of heat due to radiation. 3.3 Stand The vertical stand for the dew gauge and the base shall be of non-rusting, non-magnetic and non-corrosive stainless steel or similar material. 3.3.1 The vertical stand shall be made of tube of suitable strength. 3.3.1.1 Alternatively, the dew gauge stand can also suitably be made in two pieces so that one piece rest snugly into the other without any gap or protrusions outside, however, the total height should remain the same as shown in Fig. 1. 3.3.2 The base shall be made up of a single plate. 3.3.3 The stand shall be fixed vertically on the centre of the base plate with suitable threading arrangement into the base so that the height of the stand above the ground level shall be exactly 1 100 mm. 3.3.4 The stand shall be painted with sufficient coating of white rubber paint to prevent absorption of heat due to radiation. 3.3.5 The base of the stand shall also be painted with suftlcient coating of a suitable anti-corrosive paint. 4 DIMENSIONS AND TOLERANCES 4.1 The dimensions for the dew gauge, supports, clamp and vertical stand with base shall be as given in Fig. 2, 3 and 4 respectively. 4.2 The dimensions shall be correct to within +1 mm of the specified value given in Fig. 2, 3 and 4 respectively. 5 DESIGNATION For the purpose of inquiry or order, the wooden block, supports and vertical stand with base shall be totally designated as `Dew Gauge'. 6 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 6.1 Each rectangular block of dew gauge has to be placed on fixed supports provided at the heights of 50 mm, 250 mm, 500 mm and 1 000 mm from the ground level. The vertical heights being measured from the ground to the centre of the dew gauge. 6.2 The dew gauge supports shall be level-mounted in opposite direction alternately. 2

b) c) d) e) o

3.1.1 The rectangular blocks of wood shall be made up of only one single piece of.solid, plain teak wood, free from scratches, wrinkles, dents, cavities, hollow or holes. The material shall be such that it is capable of w ithstanding the weathering effects of exposure in open air for long period. 3.1.2 A groove each of 5 mm x 10 mm shall be made on side `B' at a distance of 48 mm from either edges of the dew gauge throughout its width so that it site firmly on the support. 3.1.3 The surfaces of the dew gauge shall not be greasy or oily or dusty. 3.1.4 The rectangular blocks of wood shall be coated with a uniform coating of suitable good quality red oxide paint several times till they are perfectly smooth in order to retain the proper deposition of dew on their surfaces. 3.2 Support and Clamp The supports and clamps for the dew gauge shall be of non-rusting, non-magnetic and non-corrosive stainless steel or similar material, 3.2.1 The supports shall be firmly level mounted on the vertical stand in opposite directions alternately by

6.3 The dew gauge stand shall be fixed perfectly vertical with the base embedded in the ground. 7 TESTING AND INSPECTION All the dew gauges shall be individually tested for conformity to all the requirements of this specification and shall carry a certificate from a competent authority to this effect. 8 MARKING shall bear the following inscription engraved legibly and neatly on a brass name plate of suitable size and shall be cemented firmly on the vertical stand: a) b) c) The inscription DEW GAUGE; Serial No. and the year of manufacture; and Manufacturer's name or recognized trademark and address.
